analysis.reason: This paper presents the first systematic study of black hole spin evolution across the continuous transition from weakly magnetized (SANE) to magnetically arrested disks (MAD) using 3D GRMHD simulations with live spacetime updates, providing an analytical subgrid prescription for spin-up/spin-down equilibria in relativistic jets and compact accretors.
analysis.result: The equilibrium spin declines steeply with normalized horizon magnetic flux $\tilde{\phi} \equiv \phi / \phi_{\rm MAD}$, dropping from $a_{\star;{\rm eq}} \approx 0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows ($\tilde{\phi} \lesssim 0.2$), through $a_{\star;{\rm eq}}(\tilde{\phi}=0.5) \approx 0.5$, down to $a_{\star;{\rm eq}} \approx 0.05\text{--}0.06$ at MAD saturation ($\tilde{\phi} = 1$). In the sustained MAD regime, the BH reaches within $3\%\text{--}6\%$ of its equilibrium spin by accreting only $\lesssim 50\%$ of its initial mass.
analysis.reading_entry: II Black hole spin evolution in a nutshell
analysis.problem: Prior GRMHD simulations assumed static black hole spacetimes and explored only binary extremes (pure SANE or saturated MAD), lacking continuous quantitative descriptions of BH spin evolution and equilibrium spins across intermediate magnetic flux levels.
analysis.method: Performed long-duration 3D GRMHD simulations with the H-AMR code tracking horizon energy and angular momentum fluxes ($dM_{\rm BH}/dt = \int T^r_t dA_{\theta\varphi}$, $dJ/dt = -\int T^r_\varphi dA_{\theta\varphi}$), updating the Kerr-Schild metric self-consistently with a moving boundary at $r_{\rm b} = 0.7 r_{\rm H}$. Numerical fits for hydrodynamical and electromagnetic fluxes yield the spin rate $s = l_{\rm HD} + l_{\rm EM} - 2a_\star(e_{\rm HD} + e_{\rm EM})$.
assumptions: Coordinate metric changes instantaneously over time steps without backreacting on external gas through non-local metric work terms ($|E_{\rm miss}| / \Delta M_{\rm BH} \lesssim 2\%\text{--}4\%$)
limits: Fitting formulae calibrated for $\tilde{\phi} \lesssim 1.2$ in radiatively inefficient thick disks; radiative cooling (e.g., in collapsars or thin disks) shifts $a_{\star;{\rm eq}}$ higher

analysis.reason: The paper develops a rigorous characteristic-function formalism to construct tractable likelihoods and optimal sufficient statistics for non-Gaussian stochastic gravitational-wave backgrounds produced by compact binary coalescences (BBH/BNS/NSBH). It directly informs searches for intermittent and popcorn-type compact object merger backgrounds relevant to high-energy transient source populations.
analysis.result: The exact non-Gaussian GWB likelihood is decoupled via Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation into the characteristic function of single mergers $z(\eta;\Lambda)$. For a toy model with segment noise $\sigma^2$, event rate $\bar{N}$, and amplitude variance $A_0^2$, the exact detection floor flattens at $\bar{N} A_0^2 \simeq 10^{-2}$ for $\bar{N} \gtrsim 10^{-2}$ and drops by a factor of $\sim 3$ toward $\bar{N} = 10^{-3}$. The single-component likelihood $\mathcal{L}_{M=1}$ is sensitive only to the degenerate combination $\bar{N} A_0^2$, whereas multi-component Gaussian mixtures $\mathcal{L}_M$ converge to the exact detection threshold with only 3 components.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first systematic study of black hole spin evolution across the continuous transition from weakly magnetized (SANE) to magnetically arrested disks (MAD) using 3D GRMHD simulations with live spacetime updates, providing an analytical subgrid prescription for spin-up/spin-down equilibria in relativistic jets and compact accretors.
analysis.result: The equilibrium spin declines steeply with normalized horizon magnetic flux $\tilde{\phi} \equiv \phi / \phi_{\rm MAD}$, dropping from $a_{\star;{\rm eq}} \approx 0.9$ in weakly magnetized flows ($\tilde{\phi} \lesssim 0.2$), through $a_{\star;{\rm eq}}(\tilde{\phi}=0.5) \approx 0.5$, down to $a_{\star;{\rm eq}} \approx 0.05\text{--}0.06$ at MAD saturation ($\tilde{\phi} = 1$). In the sustained MAD regime, the BH reaches within $3\%\text{--}6\%$ of its equilibrium spin by accreting only $\lesssim 50\%$ of its initial mass.
analysis.reading_entry: II Black hole spin evolution in a nutshell
analysis.problem: Prior GRMHD simulations assumed static black hole spacetimes and explored only binary extremes (pure SANE or saturated MAD), lacking continuous quantitative descriptions of BH spin evolution and equilibrium spins across intermediate magnetic flux levels.
analysis.method: Performed long-duration 3D GRMHD simulations with the H-AMR code tracking horizon energy and angular momentum fluxes ($dM_{\rm BH}/dt = \int T^r_t dA_{\theta\varphi}$, $dJ/dt = -\int T^r_\varphi dA_{\theta\varphi}$), updating the Kerr-Schild metric self-consistently with a moving boundary at $r_{\rm b} = 0.7 r_{\rm H}$. Numerical fits for hydrodynamical and electromagnetic fluxes yield the spin rate $s = l_{\rm HD} + l_{\rm EM} - 2a_\star(e_{\rm HD} + e_{\rm EM})$.
assumptions: Coordinate metric changes instantaneously over time steps without backreacting on external gas through non-local metric work terms ($|E_{\rm miss}| / \Delta M_{\rm BH} \lesssim 2\%\text{--}4\%$)
limits: Fitting formulae calibrated for $\tilde{\phi} \lesssim 1.2$ in radiatively inefficient thick disks; radiative cooling (e.g., in collapsars or thin disks) shifts $a_{\star;{\rm eq}}$ higher

Even at the conservative limit $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.0$, the halo metallicity exceeds pristine IGM accretion ($Z_{\mathrm{IGM}} \lesssim 0.1 \, Z_{\odot}$), whereas $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$ produces unphysical super-solar metallicities ($Z \gg 1 \, Z_{\odot}$) along multiple sightlines.
analysis.problem: Converting soft X-ray metal absorption columns (such as $\mathrm{O\,VII}$ and $\mathrm{O\,VIII}$) into total CGM gas mass suffers from an inherent degeneracy with assumed halo metallicity, leaving the true chemical enrichment and baryon content of the hot volume-filling CGM unconstrained.
analysis.method: The framework compares metallicity-dependent X-ray absorption DMs (referenced to $Z_{\mathrm{ref}} = 0.3 \, Z_{\odot}$ under collisional ionization equilibrium) to metallicity-independent FRB DMs via $Z_{\mathrm{MW,CGM}} = Z_{\mathrm{ref}} \left[ \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{metal}, Z_{\mathrm{ref}}} / \left(\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{obs}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{MW, ISM}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{cosmic}} - \mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{host}}/(1+z)\right) \right]$. Host galaxy DM contributions are sampled via Monte Carlo from a log-normal distribution with $e^{\mu_{\mathrm{host}}} = 100$ and $\sigma_{\mathrm{host}} = 1.0$, rejecting non-physical realizations with $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{MW,CGM}} \le 0$ until $10^5$ valid draws are acquired.
assumptions: The hot phase of the CGM ($T \gtrsim 10^6 \, \mathrm{K}$) is under collisional ionization equilibrium (CIE) with ionization fractions determined from O VIII to O VII ratios or upper limits.
limits: Subtracting the mean cosmic Macquart relation systematically over-corrects low-redshift sightlines ($z < 0.3$), which have fewer intervening halos, causing an over-subtraction of $\mathrm{DM}_{\mathrm{cosmic}}$ and artificially high metallicities at $f_{\mathrm{d}} = 0.8$.
